r.정치 구도: A parliamentary republic: the president is elected by parliament, while the prime minister runs the government. The two chambers have almost equal powers and the government needs the confidence of both, which helps explain why Italy has had more than 60 governments since becoming a republic in 1946. The coalition of three right-wing parties formed after the 2022 election has proved unusually durable. But its reform drive suffered a blow in March 2026, when voters rejected in a referendum a constitutional amendment to separate the careers of judges and prosecutors. Since then the government has pushed an electoral reform that gives extra seats to the bloc winning the most votes, ahead of the next general election due in 2027.

t.why: It was a founding member of both the EU and NATO and is one of the G7 economies. Its peninsula juts into the middle of the Mediterranean, so its southern islands are often the first landfall for migrants crossing by boat from Libya and Tunisia. Migration is therefore always near the center of its politics, and a deal to hold migrants in centers built in Albania has repeatedly been blocked by court rulings. In 2019 it became the first G7 country to join China's Belt and Road Initiative, then left in December 2023. Its public debt is among the highest in the eurozone, so a rise in Italian bond yields puts all of Europe's financial markets on edge.
t.rel: The Alps give it borders with France, Switzerland, Austria and Slovenia, and the Vatican and San Marino lie inside it. Across the Mediterranean it works with Libya and Tunisia to stop migrant boats. It is a founding member of the EU and a NATO member.
t.korea: Ties date back to an 1884 treaty with the Joseon kingdom, and diplomatic relations were re-established in 1956; the two countries marked 140 years of relations in 2024. During the Korean War, although Italy was not yet a UN member, it sent Red Cross Field Hospital No. 68, which treated soldiers and civilians from late 1951 to early 1955. A memorial in Busan honors the five countries, Italy among them, that sent medical units.
t.know: Two entire countries, Vatican City and San Marino, lie inside Italy.
etext: The industrial belt linking Milan and Turin is home to machinery, car, chemical and pharmaceutical plants. Many are family-run small and mid-sized firms, and many make a particular machine or component as well as anyone in the world.
Fashion, handbags, eyewear, furniture, wine and cheese all command a premium simply for being made in Italy. Tourists come in large numbers too, making tourism a major pillar of the economy.

Its public debt is the second-highest in the eurozone after Greece's, so interest costs are a constant burden. The south earns far less than the north and youth unemployment there is high, so many young people leave for the north or abroad. A low birth rate is aging the population fast, and productivity has barely grown for years.
